expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: `SubscriptionState` is inline discriminated union with four variants keyed on status: `| { readonly status: "trialing"; readonly trialEndsAt: Date } | { readonly status: "active"; readonly renewsAt: Date } ...`

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Canceled variant has {status, canceledAt, cancellation}; Trialing has {status, trialEndsAt}; no variant contains optional fields from other variants

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: `function assertNever(x: never)` used in `apply()` switch; also uses `Record<Status, readonly SubscriptionEvent["type"][]>` which breaks build when new status added

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId as `Brand<string, ...>`; RetryCount as `Brand<number, ...>` with bounds validation

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Single `apply(sub: Subscription, event: SubscriptionEvent): TransitionResult` function; `LEGAL: Readonly<Record<Status, readonly SubscriptionEvent["type"][]>>` constrains allowed transitions; 'The ONLY way to reach a new state'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists misuses with hazard codes (C8, C2, M3, F1, C1, M2); shows table mapping 'Hazard | Device | Rung': 'Nonsense field combinations | discriminated union | Control', '`voluntary` + wrong reason | nested Cancellation union | Control'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union with apply() function; C8 bag-of-optionals listed as prevented misuse
